item.title: Digital Technologies for Combating Unethical Labour Practices and Promoting Human Rights
item.content:encoded:
Stefan Gold, Technical University of Munich

Antoine Harfouche, Paris Nanterre University

Paul Jones, Swansea University

Maryam Lotfi, Cardiff University

Guoqing Zhao, Swansea University

Unethical labour practices represent a pressing global issue, with an estimated 50 million people currently living in such conditions worldwide. The prevalence of unethical labour practices is expected to increase due to ongoing regional conflicts, economic downturns, and restrictive migration policies in major Western countries. Digital technologies, such as blockchain, artificial intelligence (AI), and cloud computing, promise significant benefits in addressing unethical labour practices and have consequently attracted increasing scholarly attention.

Appel publié par Information Systems Frontiers. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Role of blockchain, artificial intelligence, and cloud computing in addressing unethical labour practices
  • Monitoring and detection of modern slavery and human trafficking using digital technologies
  • Machine learning and AI applications for identifying trafficking patterns and at-risk populations
  • Blockchain technology for supply chain transparency and labour exploitation mitigation
  • Remote sensors and worker voice technologies for identifying unethical practices in supply chains
  • Digital technologies for supporting social inclusion and reintegration of modern slavery survivors
  • Biometric recognition and satellite imagery applications by governments and NGOs
  • Digital technology adoption mechanisms for mitigating unethical labour practices
  • Theoretical and empirical frameworks for digital technology deployment in combating labour exploitation
  • Policy implications and business leadership strategies for leveraging digital technologies against unethical labour practices

Timeline

  • February 15, 2027: Submission deadline

item.title: Transformative Marketing Strategies: Embracing the Future
item.content:encoded:
V. Kumar, Brock University

The use of new-age tools for transformative marketing strategies is an emerging area with several unexplored dimensions. While prior research has established a conceptual foundation, significant gaps remain unaddressed. Existing studies primarily focus on theoretical frameworks or conceptual models, lacking sufficient empirical validation of how these technologies influence consumer attitudes, decision-making, and purchasing behavior.

Furthermore, there is a lack of empirical research quantifying the return on investment (ROI) of integrating these advanced technologies into marketing campaigns. Previous research has also not thoroughly examined the tension between hyper-personalized marketing enabled by GAI and consumer privacy concerns, particularly in the context of Blockchain's ability to ensure data traceability.

This special issue aims to encourage researchers to explore these critical issues and bridge the existing research gaps.

Appel publié par Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Use of new-age tools for transformative marketing strategies
  • Empirical validation of how technologies influence consumer attitudes, decision-making, and purchasing behavior
  • Return on investment (ROI) of integrating advanced technologies into marketing campaigns
  • Tension between hyper-personalized marketing and consumer privacy concerns
  • Blockchain's ability to ensure data traceability in marketing contexts
  • Generative AI (GAI) applications in marketing

Timeline

  • August 31, 2026: Submission deadline
